Wrong. Monitors that are freesync or gsync will work fine at high refresh rates. I have a crappy TN panel (that doesn't have adaptive sync) that does 144Hz with backlight strobing just fine. No drops to 60Hz in order to work. You are also incorrect about input lag. While it depends on what monitor you're using, generally high refresh rate displays will have lower input lag, especially at higher refresh rates (for instance my monitor has much lower input lag than most "dumb" monitors). VA (vertical alignment) has vastly superior contrast ratios to IPS (probably why many higher end TVs use VA instead of IPS) and also doesn't really have that glow that some IPS panels suffer from. 2 main reasons I got this TV is because it can do 120Hz at 1080p (or even 1440p if I want, but it doesn't look too good because of poor scaling) and because it does pixel doubling at 1080p (repeats pixels twice in each axis instead of using a not so good looking upscaler to scale to 4K).
